messages:
ryan-sales: Hey team — Pegaus POC kickoff tomorrow. Sales asked for a clear capacity plan + short security checklist for the contract. Can infra/eng confirm minimal reserved GPUs + autoscale strategy?

liz-infra: Quick numbers to start — customer expects bursty chat at ~450 qps (avg payload ~1.1k tokens). For the requested model (7B quantized), rough baseline is 1 GPU can sustain ~120 qps with our runtime under current batching. So recommend 4 reserved GPUs to hit steady 450 qps headroom ~20%. Add burst pool of 1-2 GPUs for spikes.

omar-eng: Agree with liz. Also consider KV cache warming; if many distinct prefixes, effective throughput drops ~15-25% until warmed. Plan: prewarm KV on day 0 + warmup window during POC ramp.

alex-sales: Pricing question from customer: what discount do reserved commits get vs on-demand in POC? They want monthly commit pricing and how burst credits are charged.

liz-infra: For POC we typically offer a short-term reserved rate at ~18% off on-demand for 1-3 month commits. Burst use is billed at a higher on-demand rate but we can cap monthly burst spend and report alerts.

jen-security: Security checklist quick hits: they need SOC2 controls, VPC peering for Private, KMS integration for key management, and proof of data residency (EU region). Also need answers for questionnaire Q12 (data retention) and Q24 (third-party subprocessors). I can draft responses.

ryan-sales: Thanks — can we put this into a minimal runbook we can hand to the customer? They asked for: 1) commit GPU count + burst policy, 2) autoscale triggers, 3) expected p99 latencies at target qps, 4) billing outline, 5) security items.

omar-eng: I'll add p99 latency numbers. For 450 qps target on 4xA10-like GPUs running quantized 7B: expect p95 ~120-190ms token latency, p99 for single-turn chat ~450-700ms depending on sequence length and KV cache state. If we use 6 GPUs (2 reserved burst) p99 drops ~20-30%.

liz-infra: Autoscale recommendation: reserved pool = 4 GPUs (always warm). Burst pool = +2 GPUs auto-add when queue depth > 50 requests for 30s OR token backlog > 100k tokens. Prewarm policy: during business hours allow pre-allocated warm slots to minimize cold starts.

alex-sales: Customer asked about failure modes — what happens if we run out of capacity?

liz-infra: Fallback policy: 1) Return degraded model variant (smaller quantized or CPU-fallback) with explicit header + telemetry, 2) Queue with progressive 503s + ETA, 3) Route to another region if cross-region allowed. We can commit SLA with blackout windows documented.

jen-security: On questionnaire Q12/Q24: draft answers — retention = customer-configurable, default 30 days; subprocessors list attached (cloud provider, monitoring, CDN). I'll attach the doc after this thread.

deploy-bot: deploy status: pegasus-model-7b-q4 deployed to staging GPU pool (4 replicas). Smoke tests: pass.

omar-eng: I'll produce a 1-page runbook summary with minimal config snippet for autoscale. Example config we use for POCs:

```yaml
reserved: 4
burst_max: 2
scale_up_trigger:
  - queue_depth: 50
  - token_backlog: 100000
scale_cooldown: 30s
prewarm_windows:
  - business_hours: true
```

ryan-sales: Perfect — once you add the p99 numbers + security bullet list I'll paste this into the customer email. Also flag any blockers for legal (DPA/KMS) and finance (billing cap).

liz-infra: Blockers: need confirmation of region (EU vs US) for residency + whether they require HSM-backed KMS. If HSM, private deployment may be needed and pricing changes.

alex-sales: I'll ask the customer to confirm region and HSM requirement in the kickoff.

ryan-sales: Great. Thanks everyone. Tagging @jen-security for final questionnaire doc and @liz-infra for runbook PDF. :thumbsup:
